about: The install steps: one source for /start (wizard and manual, personal: the command carries your code) and /help/ (generic: points to /start for the command). Ids are stable: the video slots and both pages key on them. Placeholders in text: {base} is the full view's address, {code} the single-use install code (on /help/, render the command as a pointer to /start). audience: start = /start only (needs a login), both = /start and /help/. Every step has check (how to know it worked) and if_not (what to do when it didn't); every troubleshooting entry ends in fix. addons: links verified in a browser on 2026-11-18 (source: curseforge or github); note is shown under the addon when set. steps.install.update: the code-free update commands (same placeholders). media: a clip's file name in docs/videos/media; name.mp4 stands for name-dark.mp4 and name-light.mp4 when those exist (the page picks the one for its theme). update_media and uninstall.media: the clips of those two sections. guide: /help/ only, the manual around the steps: what (its first line and the onboarding clip), quick (the 3 steps on its first screen, one action each), tabs (one line per tab of your page), status (checking the program sends, folded under Everything else) and page (each tab in detail, folded); a page section has id, title, body, and may have caption, points ([label, text]), os (like a step's) and media.
title: Getting started with wow-stats
intro: Six steps, about 5 minutes. After that you just play: your page updates within 5 minutes of a /reload or logout.

steps.title: Log in
steps.caption: Sign in with the link the owner sent you.
body: Sign in the way the owner told you: the account they made for you, or Battle.net when their sign-in page has the button. Your page's address is already set: the owner picked it.
steps.check: You land on this page, with your install command ready.
steps.if_not: "You're signed in, but the person who runs this site hasn't let you in yet": the owner hasn't added you yet. Tell them you signed in, then reload the page. A login loop: same message to the owner.

body: The owner sends you a link to your start page, {base}/start: this guide with your own install command in it, and a tick when each step works. Sign in the way they told you: the account they made for you, or Battle.net when their sign-in page has the button. Your page's address is already set: the owner picked it.
generic.check: Your start page opens with your install command ready.
generic.if_not: "You're signed in, but the person who runs this site hasn't let you in yet": the owner hasn't added you yet. Tell them you signed in, then reload the page. A login loop: same message to the owner.

steps.title: Install the addons
steps.caption: Polestar, and Syndicator for your gear. The install command adds Polestar Recorder.
body: Easiest: the CurseForge app (https://www.curseforge.com/download/app), which lists WoW Forever as its own install (restart the app if it doesn't). Polestar is required: your level times, quests and dungeons. Syndicator is worth adding: it tells your page what you wear and carry, so the gear advice starts from your own bags. Without it your gear comes from Battle.net, when the owner set that up. The others are optional; your start page lists what each one adds.
steps.check: Character select, AddOns: Polestar, Polestar Recorder and Syndicator are ticked, and you typed /psrec on once in game (not needed with the Polestar Client). Once data arrives (step 4), each addon turns green in the list on this page.
steps.if_not: Missing from the AddOns list: the folder is one level too deep (Interface/AddOns/Polestar/Polestar/...). Move it up so Interface/AddOns/Polestar/Polestar.toc exists, then restart WoW.

generic.check: Character select, AddOns: Polestar, Polestar Recorder and Syndicator are ticked, and you typed /psrec on once in game (not needed with the Polestar Client). Once data arrives, each addon turns green on your start page.

steps.title: Run the install command
steps.caption: One line in a terminal. No admin rights.
body: It installs a small program that sends what WoW and your addons save to your page, every 5 minutes, and adds Polestar Recorder to WoW's AddOns folder (the official release, checked) unless you have a newer one. It finds the WoW folder by itself and writes only under your user folder and to that AddOns folder.

windows.label: Windows (PowerShell)
windows.how: Windows key, type PowerShell, Enter. Paste with a right click, press Enter.
windows.installs: %LOCALAPPDATA%\wow-stats and a scheduled task "wow-stats" (every 5 minutes, as you, no admin). Log: %LOCALAPPDATA%\wow-stats\wow-stats.log. Polestar Recorder in _forever_\Interface\AddOns.

mac.label: Mac (Terminal)
mac.how: Cmd+Space, type Terminal, Enter. Paste with Cmd+V, press Enter.
mac.installs: ~/.local/share/wow-stats, ~/.config/wow-stats/config.toml and a launchd agent local.wow-stats (every 5 minutes). Log: ~/Library/Logs/wow-stats.log. Polestar Recorder in _forever_/Interface/AddOns.

steps.code_note: The command works once, within 15 minutes. Used or expired: click "Get my install command" again. You only need it once: the program updates itself.
steps.check: The output says "wow-stats is installed. WoW folder: ..." and that folder is your _forever_ folder.
steps.if_not: "WoW folder not found" or the wrong folder: see that troubleshooting entry. "This install code expired or was used already": get a new command and run it.

steps.title: Play 5 minutes
steps.caption: Play, then /reload or log out.
body: Play a few minutes, then /reload or log out: WoW saves the addons' files only then. Your page gets them within 5 minutes.
The first run sends everything your addons saved so far, every character. After that, only what's new.
A crash or Alt+F4 loses what the addons gathered since the last save: /reload after a dungeon, an Auction House scan, and before a break.
steps.check: "Data arrived" ticks on this page by itself. No refresh needed.
steps.if_not: Nothing after 10 minutes: first type /psrec on in WoW (the Recorder starts off without the Polestar Client), then /reload. Still nothing: see "My page is still empty after 10 minutes".

generic.check: "Data arrived" ticks on your start page by itself, and the program's log ends in a line like "ship: ... sent (N events)".

steps.title: See your character
steps.caption: Your character, your climb and your gear.
body: Open My page: each character you played with the addons on is in the list at the top, with level, gear and time per level.

Battle.net's copy of your characters (their look, and your gear without Syndicator) comes within minutes of your first data, then every 2 hours, if the owner set it up. Settings decides what others see: your public page stays off until you switch it on.
steps.check: Your character is in the list at the top of My page.
steps.if_not: Step 4 ticked but no character: Polestar Recorder is off for that character. Tick it in AddOns at character select, /reload, wait 5 minutes.

body: Open {base}: each character you played with the addons on is in the list at the top, with level, gear and time per level. Battle.net's copy of your characters (their look, and your gear without Syndicator) comes within minutes of your first data, then every 2 hours, if the owner set it up. Settings decides what others see: your public page stays off until you switch it on.
generic.check: Your character is in the list at the top of your page.
generic.if_not: Data arrived but no character: Polestar Recorder is off for that character. Tick it in AddOns at character select, /reload, wait 5 minutes.

steps.title: Connect your AI
steps.caption: Add wow-stats as a connector once.
body: Claude, ChatGPT or another assistant reads your stats and plans your next session: what to do in 2 hours, which gear to chase, which dungeon is worth it. It runs on your own AI account: wow-stats never sees the conversation.

claude.label: Claude (web, desktop, phone)
claude.how: Settings, Connectors, Add custom connector. Paste the address, save, then Connect and log in with this page's account.

claude-code.label: Claude Code
claude-code.how: Run this, then /mcp in Claude Code and log in.

steps.check: Ask "With wow-stats, what's my character doing?": the answer names your character.
steps.if_not: "Client Not Registered" or a disconnected connector: see that troubleshooting entry.

troubleshooting.title: My page is still empty after 10 minutes
troubleshooting.body: WoW saves the addons' files only on /reload or logout, and the program that sends your data runs every 5 minutes.
troubleshooting.fix: Type /psrec on in WoW (the Recorder starts off unless the Polestar Client installed it), then /reload and wait 5 minutes. Still nothing: read the last lines of the log (Mac ~/Library/Logs/wow-stats.log, Windows %LOCALAPPDATA%\wow-stats\wow-stats.log). "HTTP 401": the password is stale, run a new install command from your start page. "unreachable": check your connection; nothing is lost, it all goes once you are back online.

troubleshooting.title: My last session is missing
troubleshooting.body: WoW addons write their files only at logout, /reload or a clean quit. A crash, or Alt+F4, loses everything every addon gathered since the last save. No addon can save on a timer.
troubleshooting.fix: Type /reload after a dungeon, after an Auction House scan and before a break, or put /reload on a macro key. What the game never wrote can't be recovered.

troubleshooting.title: "WoW folder not found" (or the wrong folder)
troubleshooting.body: The installer looks for a _forever_ folder with WTF/ in it where Battle.net puts WoW: C:\Program Files (x86)\World of Warcraft\_forever_ on Windows (or the World of Warcraft folder Battle.net registered, on any drive), /Applications/World of Warcraft/_forever_ on a Mac. WTF/ only exists after one login.
troubleshooting.fix: Log in to WoW Forever once, quit, then run a new install command. Not sure where WoW is: in the Battle.net app, pick World of Warcraft, click the cog next to Play, then Show in Explorer (Show in Finder on a Mac); the _forever_ folder is in the World of Warcraft folder. WoW installed somewhere else: on a Mac, put `WOW_STATS_WOW_DIR="/path/to/_forever_"` before `bash` at the end of your command (`... | WOW_STATS_WOW_DIR="/path/to/_forever_" bash`); on Windows, first run `$env:WOW_STATS_WOW_DIR = 'D:\Games\World of Warcraft\_forever_'` in the same PowerShell window, then the command.

troubleshooting.title: An antivirus blocked the installer
troubleshooting.body: Some antivirus tools block `irm | iex` and unknown scheduled tasks. The installer writes only under your user folder and to WoW's AddOns folder, and adds one task that runs every 5 minutes.
troubleshooting.fix: Allow the script once from the antivirus's quarantine or history, then run a new install command. Can't allow it: send the owner a screenshot of the warning.

troubleshooting.title: "Client Not Registered" in Claude
troubleshooting.body: Claude kept a login from before the server changed.
troubleshooting.fix: Remove the wow-stats connector in Claude, add it again with the same address, and connect once more.

troubleshooting.title: Nothing arrives since a reboot
troubleshooting.body: On Windows the task starts when you log in to Windows, not at boot. On a Mac the agent loads when you log in to macOS.
troubleshooting.fix: Log in and wait 5 minutes. Still nothing: Windows, Task Scheduler, task wow-stats shows its last run and result; Mac, `launchctl print gui/$(id -u)/local.wow-stats` says whether it's loaded. Either way, a new install command from your start page replaces the job and keeps your archive.

troubleshooting.title: The AI login keeps coming back
troubleshooting.body: A login request is good for a few minutes and once. A login tab left open, or a second login started in another tab, sends you round again. A sign-in page that keeps returning means you're signed in there with an account that has no wow-stats access.
troubleshooting.fix: Close every login tab, start the connection again from the client and sign in straight away. Sign-in page loop: sign out there (or use a private window) and sign in with the account your page uses.

troubleshooting.title: My AI doesn't see the tools
troubleshooting.body: Added is not enabled: most clients connect a server but leave it off for a chat, or wait for you to log in.
troubleshooting.fix: claude.ai: turn the connector on for the chat (the tools menu under the message box). Claude Code: `/mcp` must show wow as connected, not "needs authentication". ChatGPT: developer mode on and the connector picked for the chat. VS Code: start the server from mcp.json and use agent mode. Then name it: "use wow-stats to plan my next 2 hours".

troubleshooting.title: Logged out after a server update
troubleshooting.body: An update can change the server's signing key or its tool list, and a login unused for 30 days expires. Calls then fail with 401 or "invalid token", and new tools stay hidden: clients keep the tool list for the session.
troubleshooting.fix: Log in again. claude.ai: Settings, Connectors, wow, Disconnect, then Connect. Claude Code: `/mcp`, wow, Re-authenticate. Then start a new chat to get the new tools.

needs: WoW Forever on Windows 10 or 11, or macOS, logged in once (so its WTF folder exists).
The link the owner sent you.
No admin rights: everything installs for your user only.

app.title: With the CurseForge app (recommended)
steps: Download the CurseForge app (Windows, macOS, Linux) and install it.
Pick World of Warcraft, then the Forever instance. Not listed: restart the app so it updates.
Search each addon by its exact name and click Install.

Polestar Recorder isn't on CurseForge: the install command adds it. By hand: take the Polestar_Recorder zip from its GitHub release and unzip it like the steps below, or install the Polestar Client from Polestar's site, which installs it and turns it on. Without the Client, type /psrec on in WoW once.
At character select, click AddOns (bottom left), pick the character in the drop-down at the top, tick the addons, Okay. Once per character.
Restart WoW completely: /reload doesn't load a new addon.

manual.title: By hand, from the zips
steps: On each addon's page, download its Forever file.

Unzip into the _forever_ folder's Interface/AddOns/ (Windows: C:\Program Files (x86)\World of Warcraft\_forever_\Interface\AddOns, Mac: /Applications/World of Warcraft/_forever_/Interface/AddOns) so the addon's folder sits directly inside it (Interface/AddOns/Polestar/Polestar.toc). Make the folder if it isn't there yet.

shipper.title: What the little program does
body: A small Python program that runs in the background on the computer you play on, every 5 minutes. It never touches the game: it reads the files WoW writes on /reload or logout.

Each run turns what's new in your WTF folder into events and posts them to your page with your own upload password; a copy of what it sent stays in WoWArchive in your home folder. With Git installed (Macs often have it), it also keeps every version of the WTF folder there. Nothing is sent twice; offline, it waits for the next run.
The first run sends your whole history: everything your addons saved so far.
sends: your addons' saved files (SavedVariables), every character
WoW's combat logs, when there are any

update: Addons: Update all in the CurseForge app.

The program on your computer updates itself, and Polestar Recorder with it, within a few hours of a new version on the server. Nothing to run, nothing to reinstall. Only an install from before version 0.5.1 needs the update line once: your start page says so when yours does.
New computer, or your upload password leaked: Reset my upload password on your start page, then run the install command it gives you. The old password stops at once.

body: Run the line for your OS. It stops the job and removes the program and your config. Your addons stay, Polestar Recorder included: remove them in CurseForge, or delete their folders in _forever_/Interface/AddOns.

Your archive (WoWArchive in your home folder) stays: delete it yourself if you don't want the history. To delete your data on the site, ask the owner to take you off the friends list: it goes within minutes.

what.title: Your WoW character, and what to do next
body: Your next upgrade and where it drops, the dungeon worth running, your pace per level. Set it up once, then just play: the page fills in by itself.

quick.title: Get started in 3 steps
quick.caption: On the computer you play on. About 5 minutes.

steps.title: Install the addons
steps.body: In the CurseForge app, pick World of Warcraft, then Forever, and install:

steps.title: Run your install command
steps.body: Open your start page on that computer, log in, and copy your command. It also installs Polestar Recorder. Then:

steps.title: Play
steps.body: Type /psrec on once in game. Your page fills in a few minutes after you log out of a character.

tabs: your pace, hours to the next level, your next 3 moves.
your gear, the best upgrade per slot and where it drops, dungeons worth running, a session plan.
every level, death and session, and how you looked at each level.
top right: hide a character, share your zogzog link, turn on your public page.

status.title: Check that it sends your data
body: Read the end of its log: each run writes what it did. A good run ends in a line like "ship: ... sent (120 events)"; a run with nothing new to send writes almost nothing.
To skip the 5-minute wait, run it now with the second line: it prints nothing and writes the log.

mac.label: Mac (Terminal)
mac.how: The log, then a run by hand. The third line says whether the background job is loaded ("state = running" or "not running" between runs are both fine).
mac.command:
tail -n 20 ~/Library/Logs/wow-stats.log
uv run --script ~/.local/share/wow-stats/wow_stats.py
launchctl print gui/$(id -u)/local.wow-stats | grep -E 'state|last exit'

windows.label: Windows (PowerShell)
windows.how: The log, then a run by hand. The third line shows the task's last and next run.
windows.command:
Get-Content "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\wow-stats\wow-stats.log" -Tail 20
uv run --script "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\wow-stats\wow_stats.py"
Get-ScheduledTask -TaskName wow-stats | Get-ScheduledTaskInfo

page.title: Overview
page.caption: Open it before you log in.
body: The first tab. The line at the top says where you stand against Polestar's route and how much play the next level needs. Below it, the four numbers and your next moves.
Do the first next move. When something blocks it (your level, your gold), the move says what, and how far you are.
points: your time per level against Polestar's route, over the last 5 levels. 1.0x is the route's pace, 2.0x twice as long.
hours of play to the next level, at your XP per hour.
how many guide steps you did in order, and how many you passed over.
the rested XP you have banked. Log out in an inn or a city and it grows.
up to 3 things to do now: an upgrade and where it drops, a dungeon and the drops you'd wear, a profession rank or riding with its trainer and price. "1 more" opens the rest.
bars are your played time per level, dashes the route's.

page.title: Character
page.caption: Your gear, your climb, everything recorded.
body: The second tab. At the top, the character sheet: gear and item level, professions, talents and how they changed (every change with WoWSims Exporter, else the last 3 weeks). Hover or tap an item for its card; the Wowhead link opens its page.
Under the sheet, a bar of sections. Each one jumps to its part of the page.
points: per slot, the best item you can wear now and within 3 levels, the points it adds and where it drops. One you already carry says "In your bags: equip it".
time per level, yours against the route.
the steps that took longest against the route.
what dropped, where you died and at what level, the players you keep running into, where you flew.

page.title: Dungeons
page.caption: Which dungeon is worth it, and what it drops for you.
body: In the Character tab. Each dungeon for your level shows its level range, the drops that are upgrades for you (slot and points) and your runs: when, at what level, how long. A drop you already have says so, and whether to equip it.
Pick the one with the most upgrades you'd wear. The Overview's next moves already do: the dungeon there is that one.

page.title: Plan your next hours
page.caption: Pick the hours, get the plan.
body: In the Character tab, under the sheet: pick 1 to 6 hours, add what you don't want ("no dungeons") and click Plan it. The plan follows your Polestar guide at your own pace: the steps to do, your level at the end, the steps worth skipping, a dungeon if you find a group, where to log out.
It needs your Polestar guide steps: a character that never followed a guide gets no plan. The same box shows the gold you have toward riding and how many hours of play it takes at your rate.
To have it explained or changed, ask your AI (the Your AI part of this page).

page.title: Timeline and Journal
page.caption: Your play, back in time.
body: Timeline: every level, death, dungeon and session, newest first. Pick one to see your character then: the gear you wore, the zones, the best upgrades at the time.

Level by level: slide through your levels to see what your character looked like at each one, as a picture, or in 3D with View in 3D. A new level's picture takes a few minutes: until then it says "Picture on its way".
Journal: one entry per play session, where you went and what you did.

page.title: Your other characters
body: The picker at the top left switches character. Every character you played with the addons on is in it, alts included. One is missing: its addons are off (step 2, once per character).

page.title: Your zogzog link
page.caption: The whole story, for the friends you pick.
body: Settings has your zogzog link: your page for friends, with the journal, the gear advice, prices and deaths per zone. Anyone with the link can open it, so send it only to people you want there. It never shows other players or where your character is now.
It catches up within about 10 minutes of a play session.
Sent to the wrong person: Settings, Make a new link. The old one stops working at the next update.

page.title: Your public page
body: Off until you switch it on (Settings, Public page on). Then anyone with the address sees your characters' card, climb and dungeons. No gold, no other players, no position.
The owner adds its address once, usually within a day. Settings says "live" when it works.

page.title: Settings
page.caption: What others see, your upload password, and leaving.
body: Settings is in the menu at the top right of your page. Your own page always shows everything: these only change what others see.
points: tick it under Characters: off the public page, off the zogzog link, or both.
on, your AI gets your characters' Battle.net data (look, item level, talents) and the WoW Token price. Off, it doesn't.
new computer, or the password leaked: Reset my upload password. The old one stops at once; run the new install command on the computer you play on.

ask the owner to take you off the friends list. Within minutes your events, settings, upload password and pages are gone; backups expire on their own (the Privacy page says when). Then uninstall the program.
